XZ Utils
========

Overview
--------

XZ Utils provide a general-purpose data-compression library plus
command-line tools. The native file format is the .xz format, but
also the legacy .lzma format is supported. The .xz format supports
multiple compression algorithms, which are called "filters" in the
context of XZ Utils. The primary filter is currently LZMA2. With
typical files, XZ Utils create about 30% smaller files than gzip.

The .xz format supports multiple compression algorithms. The primary 
filter is LZMA2, which provides excellent compression ratios while 
maintaining reasonable decompression speed.

Key Features
------------

- Compresses data into the .xz format (and legacy .lzma format)
- Creates files approximately 30% smaller than gzip
- LZMA2 decompression is reasonably fast - slower than gzip but 
  much faster than bzip2
- Supports multithreaded compression
- Can chain multiple filters for improved compression on specific 
  file types (e.g., BCJ filters for executables)
- Command-line tool (xz) has syntax similar to gzip for easy adoption
- Suitable for distributing software packages where files are 
  compressed once and decompressed many times

Usage
-----

The main command-line tool is 'xz'. Common usage:

Compress a file:
    xz file.txt
    (creates file.txt.xz and removes file.txt)

Decompress a file:
    xz -d file.txt.xz
    or: unxz file.txt.xz
    (creates file.txt and removes file.txt.xz)

Keep the original file:
    xz -k file.txt

Compress to stdout:
    xz -c file.txt > file.txt.xz

Decompress to stdout:
    xz -dc file.txt.xz
    or: xzcat file.txt.xz

Test compressed file integrity:
    xz -t file.txt.xz

List information about compressed file:
    xz -l file.txt.xz

Set compression level (1-9, default 6):
    xz -6 file.txt     # balanced
    xz -9 file.txt     # maximum compression (slow, uses more memory)
    xz -1 file.txt     # fast compression

Use multithreaded compression:
    xz -T4 file.txt    # use 4 threads
    xz -T0 file.txt    # use all available CPU cores

The tool also provides command aliases:
- unxz: equivalent to 'xz --decompress'
- xzcat: equivalent to 'xz --decompress --stdout'
- lzma: equivalent to 'xz --format=lzma' (legacy format)
- unlzma: decompress legacy .lzma files
- lzcat: decompress legacy .lzma files to stdout

Additional Information
----------------------

For detailed information about the .xz file format specification, 
see doc/xz-file-format.txt

For frequently asked questions, see doc/faq.txt

For historical information about the format, see doc/history.txt

For legacy .lzma format information, see doc/lzma-file-format.txt

License
-------

XZ Utils are released under multiple licenses. See the COPYING file
and individual COPYING.* files for details.

Contact
-------

Home page: https://tukaani.org/xz/
Email: xz@tukaani.org
IRC: #tukaani on Libera Chat
GitHub: https://github.com/tukaani-project/xz
=== NEWS ===
XZ Utils Release History
=========================

This file has been simplified to show only user-facing changes.
For full development history, see the original repository.

The XZ Utils project provides data compression tools using the LZMA2
algorithm and the .xz file format. Each release has included various
improvements to compression performance, decompression speed, and
command-line tool functionality.

Major features added over the project's history include:
- Multithreaded compression support
- Various compression filters (BCJ, Delta, etc.)
- Improved memory efficiency
- Enhanced compatibility with various platforms
- Support for the .lz format (lzip decompression)
- Numerous command-line options for fine-tuning compression

For the most current version and detailed release notes,
visit: https://tukaani.org/xz/

        If an implementation supports handling .xz files with multiple

2.1.1. Stream Header

        +---+---+---+---+---+---+-------+------+--+--+--+--+
        |  Header Magic Bytes   | Stream Flags |   CRC32   |
        +---+---+---+---+---+---+-------+------+--+--+--+--+


2.1.1.1. Header Magic Bytes

        The first six (6) bytes of the Stream are so called Header
        Magic Bytes. They can be used to identify the file type.

            Using a C array and ASCII:
            const uint8_t HEADER_MAGIC[6]
                    = { 0xFD, '7', 'z', 'X', 'Z', 0x00 };

            In plain hexadecimal:
            FD 37 7A 58 5A 00

        Notes:
          - The first byte (0xFD) was chosen so that the files cannot
            be erroneously detected as being in .lzma format, in which
            the first byte is in the range [0x00, 0xE0].
          - The sixth byte (0x00) was chosen to prevent applications
            from misdetecting the file as a text file.

        If the Header Magic Bytes don't match, the decoder MUST
        indicate an error.

import sys,struct
def vi(b,p):
    v=0;sh=0
    while True:
        c=b[p];p+=1; v|=(c&0x7f)<<sh
        if not c&0x80: return v,p
        sh+=7
def go(data):
    assert data[:6]==b'\xfd7zXZ\x00'
    off=12
    res=[]
    while True:
        bhs=data[off]
        if bhs==0:
            # index
            idx=off
            p=off+1
            n,p=vi(data,p)
            recs=[]
            for _ in range(n):
                u,p=vi(data,p); c,p=vi(data,p); recs.append((u,c))
            # padding
            end=off
            # backward size from footer
            bs=struct.unpack('<I',data[-8:-4])[0]
            isize=(bs+1)*4
            print("index at",idx,"size",isize,"recs",recs)
            return
        hdr_end=off+(bhs+1)*4
        print("blockhdr",(bhs+1)*4,"flags",hex(data[off+1]))
        # parse varints
        p=off+2
        v=None
        if data[off+1]&0x40:
            v,p=vi(data,p); print(" comp",v)
        if data[off+1]&0x80:
            u,p=vi(data,p); print(" uncomp",u)
        fid,p=vi(data,p); ps,p=vi(data,p); props=data[p:p+ps]; p+=ps
        print(" filter",hex(fid),props.hex())
        # skip to check: use index? just continue to next record using filter chain later
        # We'll parse chunks in raw mode caller
        return
d=sys.stdin.buffer.read()
go(d)

import struct,zlib,sys
def varint(v):
    out=bytearray()
    while True:
        b=v&0x7f; v>>=7
        if v: out.append(b|0x80)
        else: out.append(b); break
    return bytes(out)
def crc64(data):
    # ECMA-182 reflected, poly 0x42F0E1EBA0EA2FA9 (reversed 0xC96C5795D7870F42)
    poly=0xC96C5795D7870F42
    crc=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF
    for b in data:
        crc^=b
        for _ in range(8):
            crc=(crc>>1)^poly if crc&1 else crc>>1
    return crc^0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF
def crc32(data):
    return zlib.crc32(data)&0xffffffff
def sha256(data):
    import hashlib
    return hashlib.sha256(data).digest()
def crc_any(data,typ):
    if typ==0: return b''
    if typ==1: return struct.pack('<I',crc32(data))
    if typ==4: return struct.pack('<Q',crc64(data))
    if typ==0x0a: return sha256(data)
    raise Exception
def build(payload, check=4, compsize=None, uncompsize=None, filters=b'\x21\x01\x16'):
    # block header
    hdr=bytearray()
    flags=0
    body=bytearray()
    if compsize is not None:
        flags|=0x40; body+=varint(compsize)
    if uncompsize is not None:
        flags|=0x80; body+=varint(uncompsize)
    body+=filters
    total=2+len(body)+4
    pad=(-total)%4
    hdr.append(((total+pad)//4)-1)
    hdr.append(flags)
    hdr+=body
    hdr+=b'\x00'*pad
    hdr+=struct.pack('<I',crc32(bytes(hdr)))
    block=bytes(hdr)+payload
    block+=b'\x00'*((-len(payload))%4)
    check=crc_any(b'x'*0,check)  # placeholder
    return block
def full(payload, check=4, uncompressed=b'', filters=b'\x21\x01\x16'):
    hdr=bytearray()
    body=bytearray()
    body+=filters
    total=2+len(body)+4
    pad=(-total)%4
    hdr.append(((total+pad)//4)-1)
    hdr.append(0)
    hdr+=body
    hdr+=b'\x00'*pad
    hdr+=struct.pack('<I',crc32(bytes(hdr)))
    blk=bytes(hdr)+payload+b'\x00'*((-len(payload))%4)+crc_any(uncompressed,check)
    unpadded=len(blk)
    idx=bytearray()
    idx.append(0)
    idx+=varint(1)
    idx+=varint(unpadded)
    idx+=varint(len(uncompressed))
    while len(idx)%4: idx.append(0)
    idx+=struct.pack('<I',crc32(bytes(idx)))
    out=bytearray()
    out+=b'\xfd7zXZ\x00'+bytes([0,check])+struct.pack('<I',crc32(bytes([0,check])))
    out+=blk+idx
    out+=struct.pack('<I',crc32(bytes(idx[-8:]))+0)
    # footer: crc32 over backward size + flags
    bw=varint2(len(idx)) if False else (len(idx)//4-1)
    footer=struct.pack('<I',crc32(struct.pack('<I',bw)+bytes([0,check])))
    out+=footer+struct.pack('<I',bw)+bytes([0,check])+b'YZ'
    return bytes(out)
def varint2(v):
    out=bytearray()
    while True:
        b=v&0x7f; v>>=7
        if v: out.append(b|0x80)
        else: out.append(b); break
    return bytes(out)
EOF

1.1. Header

        +------------+----+----+----+----+--+--+--+--+--+--+--+--+
        | Properties |  Dictionary Size  |   Uncompressed Size   |
        +------------+----+----+----+----+--+--+--+--+--+--+--+--+


1.1.1. Properties

        The Properties field contains three properties. An abbreviation
        is given in parentheses, followed by the value range of the
        property. The field consists of

            1) the number of literal context bits (lc, [0, 8]);
            2) the number of literal position bits (lp, [0, 4]); and
            3) the number of position bits (pb, [0, 4]).

        The properties are encoded using the following formula:

            Properties = (pb * 5 + lp) * 9 + lc

        The following C code illustrates a straightforward way to
        decode the Properties field:

            uint8_t lc, lp, pb;
            uint8_t prop = get_lzma_properties();
            if (prop > (4 * 5 + 4) * 9 + 8)
                return LZMA_PROPERTIES_ERROR;

            pb = prop / (9 * 5);
            prop -= pb * 9 * 5;
            lp = prop / 9;
            lc = prop - lp * 9;

        XZ Utils has an additional requirement: lc + lp <= 4. Files
        which don't follow this requirement cannot be decompressed
        with XZ Utils. Usually this isn't a problem since the most
        common lc/lp/pb values are 3/0/2. It is the only lc/lp/pb
        combination that the files created by LZMA Utils can have,
        but LZMA Utils can decompress files with any lc/lp/pb.


1.1.2. Dictionary Size

        Dictionary Size is stored as an unsigned 32-bit little endian
        integer. Any 32-bit value is possible, but for maximum
        portability, only sizes of 2^n and 2^n + 2^(n-1) should be
        used.

        LZMA Utils creates only files with dictionary size 2^n,
        16 <= n <= 25. LZMA Utils can decompress files with any
        dictionary size.

        XZ Utils creates and decompresses .lzma files only with
        dictionary sizes 2^n and 2^n + 2^(n-1). If some other
        dictionary size is specified when compressing, the value
        stored in the Dictionary Size field is a rounded up, but the
        specified value is still used in the actual compression code.


1.1.3. Uncompressed Size

        Uncompressed Size is stored as unsigned 64-bit little endian
        integer. A special value of 0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF indicates
        that Uncompressed Size is unknown. End of Payload Marker (*)
        is used if Uncompressed Size is unknown. End of Payload Marker
        is allowed but rarely used if Uncompressed Size is known.
        XZ Utils 5.2.5 and older don't support .lzma files that have
        End of Payload Marker together with a known Uncompressed Size.

        XZ Utils rejects files whose Uncompressed Size field specifies
        a known size that is 256 GiB or more. This is to reject false
        positives when trying to guess if the input file is in the
        .lzma format. When Uncompressed Size is unknown, there is no
        limit for the uncompressed size of the file.

        (*) Some tools use the term End of Stream (EOS) marker
            instead of End of Payload Marker.

check_size=8

p=istart+1

import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp/t')
import mk,struct,subprocess

d=r.stdout
hdrsz=(d[12]+1)*4
bs=struct.unpack('<I',d[-8:-4])[0]; isize=(bs+1)*4; istart=len(d)-12-isize
def vi(b,p):
    v=0;sh=0
    while True:
        c=b[p];p+=1; v|=(c&0x7f)<<sh
        if not c&0x80: return v,p
        sh+=7
p=istart+1
n,p=vi(d,p); recs=[]
for _ in range(n):
    u,p=vi(d,p); c,p=vi(d,p); recs.append((u,c))
u,c=recs[0]; compsz=u-hdrsz-8
comp=d[12+hdrsz:12+hdrsz+compsz]
ctl=comp[0]
un=(((ctl&0x1f)<<16)|(comp[1]<<8|comp[2]))+1
pk=(comp[3]<<8|comp[4])+1
i=5
pb=None
if ctl&0x20: pb=comp[i]; i+=1
stream=comp[i:i+pk]
print('ctl',hex(ctl),'un',un,'pk',pk,'props',hex(pb))
# rebuild an .xz with the same chunk
props_byte = pb if pb is not None else 0x5d
payload = bytes([0xE0]) + un.to_bytes(3,'big')[1:] + (pk-1).to_bytes(2,'big') + bytes([props_byte]) + stream + b'\x00'
# wait: unpacked-1 must fit: control holds bits 16-20
hi = (un-1) >> 16

ctl_new = 0x80 | 0x40 | 0x20 | hi
payload = bytes([ctl_new]) + lo.to_bytes(2,'big') + (pk-1).to_bytes(2,'big') + bytes([props_byte]) + stream + b'\x00'
print('payload',payload.hex())
f=mk.full(payload,4,data,b'\x21\x01\x10')  # dict=1MiB props 0x10
open('/tmp/t/al/rec.xz','wb').write(f)
r2=subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable','-dc','/tmp/t/al/rec.xz'],capture_output=True)
print('rc',r2.returncode,'match',r2.stdout==data,'err',r2.stderr.decode().strip())
PY"}

        print('.lz props=%d %s rc=%d outlen=%d err=%s'%(props,sizepos,r.returncode,len(r.stdout),r.stderr.decode().strip().split(': ')[-1]))

import struct,subprocess
def extract(data,opts=None):
    open('data.bin','wb').write(data)
    args=['/workspace/executable']+([opts] if opts else [])+['-T1','-c','data.bin']
    r=subprocess.run(args,capture_output=True)

    hdrsz=(d[12]+1)*4
    bs=struct.unpack('<I',d[-8:-4])[0]; isize=(bs+1)*4; istart=len(d)-12-isize
    def vi(b,p):
        v=0;sh=0
        while True:
            c=b[p];p+=1; v|=(c&0x7f)<<sh
            if not c&0x80: return v,p
            sh+=7
    p=istart+1
    n,p=vi(d,p); recs=[]
    for _ in range(n):
        u,p=vi(d,p); c,p=vi(d,p); recs.append((u,c))
    u,c=recs[0]; compsz=u-hdrsz-8
    comp=d[12+hdrsz:12+hdrsz+compsz]
    ctl=comp[0]
    un=(((ctl&0x1f)<<16)|(comp[1]<<8|comp[2]))+1
    pk=(comp[3]<<8|comp[4])+1
    i=5
    pb=None
    if ctl&0x20: pb=comp[i]; i+=1
    return comp[i:i+pk], un, pb

import struct,subprocess,zlib
def extract(data,opts=None):
    open('data.bin','wb').write(data)
    args=['/workspace/executable']+([opts] if opts else [])+['-T1','-c','data.bin']
    r=subprocess.run(args,capture_output=True)
    d=r.stdout
    hdrsz=(d[12]+1)*4
    bs=struct.unpack('<I',d[-8:-4])[0]; isize=(bs+1)*4; istart=len(d)-12-isize
    def vi(b,p):
        v=0;sh=0
        while True:
            c=b[p];p+=1; v|=(c&0x7f)<<sh
            if not c&0x80: return v,p
            sh+=7
    p=istart+1
    n,p=vi(d,p); recs=[]
    for _ in range(n):
        u,p=vi(d,p); c,p=vi(d,p); recs.append((u,c))
    u,c=recs[0]; compsz=u-hdrsz-8
    comp=d[12+hdrsz:12+hdrsz+compsz]
    ctl=comp[0]
    un=(((ctl&0x1f)<<16)|(comp[1]<<8|comp[2]))+1
    pk=(comp[3]<<8|comp[4])+1
    i=5
    pb=None
    if ctl&0x20: pb=comp[i]; i+=1
    return comp[i:i+pk], un, pb
data=b'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. 0123456789 '*4

def encode_eopm(rc, probs, is_match, is_rep, pos_state, state=0):
    """Encode an end-of-payload marker (dist = 0xFFFFFFFF)."""
    rc.encode_bit(is_match, (state<<4)+pos_state, 1)
    rc.encode_bit(is_rep, state, 0)
    # length = 2  (len_choice=0, low tree value 0)
    rc.encode_bit(probs, 0 + 0, 0)   # len_choice
    sym=1
    for _ in range(3):
        rc.encode_bit(probs, 0+sym, 0)
        sym=(sym<<1)
    # pos_slot = 63
    base=676  # pos_slot offset in the decoder layout; encoder layout differs, use its own array
    return rc

def encode_literals_eopm(data, lc=3, lp=0, pb=2):
    rc=RE()
    nlit=0x300<<(lc+lp)
    lprobs=[1024]*nlit
    is_match=[1024]*(12<<4)
    is_rep=[1024]*12
    len_choice=[1024]
    len_low=[[1024]*8 for _ in range(16)]
    pos_slot=[1024]*64
    pos_align=[1024]*4
    pos_special=[1024]*(1+16384-14)
    pos_mask=(1<<pb)-1; lp_mask=(1<<lp)-1
    prev=0; state=0
    for i,b in enumerate(data):
        pos=i; pos_state=pos&pos_mask
        rc.encode_bit(is_match,(state<<4)+pos_state,0)
        lit_state=((pos&lp_mask)<<lc)+(prev>>(8-lc))
        base=lit_state*0x300
        sym=1
        for k in range(7,-1,-1):
            bit=(b>>k)&1
            rc.encode_bit(lprobs, base+sym, bit)
            sym=(sym<<1)|bit
        prev=b
    # EOPM
    pos=len(data); pos_state=pos&pos_mask
    rc.encode_bit(is_match,(state<<4)+pos_state,1)
    rc.encode_bit(is_rep,state,0)
    # length 2: choice bit 0, low tree value 0 (3 bits)
    rc.encode_bit(len_choice,0,0)
    sym=1
    for _ in range(3):
        rc.encode_bit(len_low[pos_state], sym, 0)
        sym=sym<<1
    # pos_slot 63: 6 bits all 1
    sym=1
    for _ in range(6):
        rc.encode_bit(pos_slot, sym, 1)
        sym=(sym<<1)|1
    # 26 direct bits all 1
    rc.encode_direct(26, 0x3FFFFFF)
    # align 4 reverse bits all 1: tree_reverse with value 15
    probe=1
    for i in range(4):
        rc.encode_bit(pos_align, probe, 1)
        probe=(probe<<1)|1
    rc.flush()
    return bytes(rc.out)

def encode_eopm(rc, probs, is_match, is_rep, pos_state, state=0):
    """Encode an end-of-payload marker (dist = 0xFFFFFFFF)."""
    rc.encode_bit(is_match, (state<<4)+pos_state, 1)
    rc.encode_bit(is_rep, state, 0)
    # length = 2  (len_choice=0, low tree value 0)
    rc.encode_bit(probs, 0 + 0, 0)   # len_choice

    for _ in range(3):

        sym=(sym<<1)
    # pos_slot = 63
    base=676  # pos_slot offset in the decoder layout; encoder layout differs, use its own array
    return rc

def encode_literals_eopm(data, lc=3, lp=0, pb=2):
    rc=RE()
    nlit=0x300<<(lc+lp)
    lprobs=[1024]*nlit
    is_match=[1024]*(12<<4)
    is_rep=[1024]*12
    len_choice=[1024]
    len_low=[[1024]*8 for _ in range(16)]
    pos_slot=[1024]*64
    pos_align=[1024]*4
    pos_special=[1024]*(1+16384-14)
    pos_mask=(1<<pb)-1; lp_mask=(1<<lp)-1
    prev=0; state=0
    for i,b in enumerate(data):

        rc.encode_bit(is_match,(state<<4)+pos_state,0)
        lit_state=((pos&lp_mask)<<lc)+(prev>>(8-lc))
        base=lit_state*0x300
        sym=1
        for k in range(7,-1,-1):
            bit=(b>>k)&1
            rc.encode_bit(lprobs, base+sym, bit)
            sym=(sym<<1)|bit
        prev=b
    # EOPM
    pos=len(data); pos_state=pos&pos_mask
    rc.encode_bit(is_match,(state<<4)+pos_state,1)
    rc.encode_bit(is_rep,state,0)
    # length 2: choice bit 0, low tree value 0 (3 bits)
    rc.encode_bit(len_choice,0,0)
    sym=1
    for _ in range(3):
        rc.encode_bit(len_low[pos_state], sym, 0)
        sym=sym<<1
    # pos_slot 63: 6 bits all 1
    sym=1
    for _ in range(6):
        rc.encode_bit(pos_slot, sym, 1)
        sym=(sym<<1)|1

    probe=1

import subprocess,struct,random
random.seed(5)
def chunks(data):
    open('cc.bin','wb').write(data)
    r=subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable','-T1','-c','cc.bin'],capture_output=True)
    d=r.stdout
    hdrsz=(d[12]+1)*4
    bs=struct.unpack('<I',d[-8:-4])[0]; isize=(bs+1)*4; istart=len(d)-12-isize
    def vi(b,p):
        v=0;sh=0
        while True:
            c=b[p];p+=1; v|=(c&0x7f)<<sh
            if not c&0x80: return v,p
            sh+=7
    p=istart+1
    n,p=vi(d,p); recs=[]
    for _ in range(n):
        u,p=vi(d,p); c,p=vi(d,p); recs.append((u,c))
    u,c=recs[0]; compsz=u-hdrsz-8
    comp=d[12+hdrsz:12+hdrsz+compsz]
    out=[]
    i=0
    while comp[i]!=0:
        ctl=comp[i]
        if ctl in (1,2):
            sz=(comp[i+1]<<8|comp[i+2])+1
            out.append(('uncomp',sz)); i+=3+sz
        else:
            un=(((ctl&0x1f)<<16)|(comp[i+1]<<8|comp[i+2]))+1
            pk=(comp[i+3]<<8|comp[i+4])+1
            out.append(('comp',un,pk)); i+=5+(6 if ctl&0x20 else 0)+pk
    return out
for nval in [2,3,4,8,16,64,256]:
    data=bytes(random.randrange(nval) for _ in range(1048576))
    r=chunks(data)
    print('nval=%-4d'%nval, r[:4])

	const uint32_t mi = (d->state << LZMA_POS_STATES_MAX) + pos_state;

				<< d->lc) + (prev_byte >> (8 - d->lc));
		probability *lprobs = d->lit + ((size_t)lit_state << 8) + lit_state;
		uint32_t symbol = 1;
		if (d->state >= LZMA_LIT_STATES) {
			const uint32_t r0 = d->reps[0];
			if ((uint64_t)d->dict_pos <= r0)

			if (d->buf_pos <= r0)

			uint32_t match_byte = d->dict[d->buf_pos - 1 - r0];
			do {
				const uint32_t match_bit = (match_byte >> 7) & 1;
				match_byte <<= 1;

				d->state, (unsigned long long)d->src.consumed);

import struct
def vi(b,p):
    v=0;sh=0
    while True:
        c=b[p];p+=1; v|=(c&0x7f)<<sh
        if not c&0x80: return v,p
        sh+=7

bs=struct.unpack('<I',d[-8:-4])[0]; isize=(bs+1)*4; istart=len(d)-12-isize
p=istart+1

off=12

    u,c=recs[k]

    print('block %d hdrsz=%d flags=%02x uncomp=%d compsz=%d'%(k,hdrsz,d[off+1],c,compsz))
    print('   hdr:', d[off:off+hdrsz].hex())
    off += hdrsz + compsz + ((4-compsz%4)%4) + 8
PY

                        ln=(sym-256 if sym>=256 else sym)+18
                print('len',ln)

lzma1_stream_decode(file_r *fr, sink *out, uint32_t lc, uint32_t lp,
		uint32_t pb, uint32_t dict_size, uint64_t known_size,
		int nofilter)
{
	block_out bo;
	memset(&bo, 0, sizeof(bo));
	bo.out = out;
	bo.nofilter = nofilter;
	bo.n_filters = 0;
	check_init_state(&bo.chk, CHECK_NONE);

	lzma_dec d;
	memset(&d, 0, sizeof(d));
	d.out_ctx = &bo;
	d.emit = block_put;
	if (lzma_dec_reset(&d, lc, lp, pb, dict_size, &bo, block_put))
		return E_MEM;
	if (lzma_dec_alloc_dict(&d, dict_size))
		return E_MEM;
	if (lzma_dec_alloc_probs(&d))
		return E_MEM;
	lz1_ctx ctx;
	ctx.fr = fr;
	rd_init(&d.src, lz1_fill, &ctx);
	d.out_limit = known_size == UINT64_MAX ? 0 : known_size;
	d.expect_end_marker = known_size == UINT64_MAX;

	int ret = lzma_dec_run(&d);
	if (ret == E_OK)
		ret = E_DATA;
	if (ret == E_BUF && d.dict_pos == known_size)
		ret = E_STREAM_END;
	lzma_dec_free_dict(&d);
	if (ret != E_STREAM_END)
		return ret;
	lzma_dec_flush_out(&d);
	if (block_flush(&bo))
		return E_MEM;
	/* push back unread bytes */
	{
		const size_t left = d.src.len - d.src.pos;
		if (left > 0) {
			uint8_t tmp[8192];
			memcpy(tmp, d.src.buf + d.src.pos, left);
			if (fr_push(fr, tmp, left))
				return E_DATA;
		}
	}
	return E_OK;
}
</output>

            reps[3]=reps[2]; reps[2]=reps[1]; reps[1]=reps[0]; reps[0]=dist
            for _ in range(ln): out.append(out[len(out)-1-dist])

enc_run(lz1e *e, size_t end)
{
	while (e->pos < end) {
		const size_t pos = e->pos;
		uint32_t dist = 0;
		uint32_t len = mf_find(e, &dist, pos, e->nice_len, e->depth);
		if (len == 0) {
			enc_literal(e, e->buf[pos]);
			mf_insert(e, pos);
			continue;
		}
		const uint32_t pos_state = (uint32_t)pos & e->pos_mask;
		rc_bit(&e->rc, &e->p.is_match[(e->state << LZMA_POS_STATES_MAX)
				+ pos_state], 1);
		/* prefer rep0 when it gives the same length */
		int is_rep = 0;
		if (e->reps[0] < e->dict_size && pos > e->reps[0]
				&& e->reps[0] < pos) {
			const uint32_t r = e->reps[0] + 1;
			uint32_t l = 0;
			while (l < len && pos + l < e->len
					&& e->buf[pos + l] == e->buf[pos - r + l])
				++l;
			if (l == len)
				is_rep = 1;
		}
		if (is_rep) {
			rc_bit(&e->rc, &e->p.is_rep[e->state], 1);
			rc_bit(&e->rc, &e->p.is_rep0[(e->state
					<< LZMA_POS_STATES_MAX) + pos_state], 0);
</output>

/* ---------------- LZMA1 stream decoding ---------------- */

typedef struct {
	file_r *fr;
} lz1_ctx;

static int
lz1_fill(reader *r)
{
	lz1_ctx *c = r->ctx;
	file_r *fr = c->fr;
	if (fr->eof)
		return 0;
	size_t want = sizeof(r->buf) - r->pos;
	if (want > 8192)
		want = 8192;
	if (want == 0)
		return 0;
	const size_t n = fr_read(fr, r->buf + r->pos, want);
	r->len = r->pos + n;
	return n > 0;
}

/* Decode a raw LZMA1 stream (no header).  known_size: uncompressed size if
 * known, otherwise UINT64_MAX.  Returns E_* . */
int
lzma1_stream_decode(file_r *fr, sink *out, uint32_t lc, uint32_t lp,
		uint32_t pb, uint32_t dict_size, uint64_t known_size,
		int nofilter)
{
	block_out bo;
	memset(&bo, 0, sizeof(bo));
	bo.out = out;
	bo.nofilter = nofilter;
	bo.n_filters = 0;
	check_init_state(&bo.chk, CHECK_NONE);

	lzma_dec d;
	memset(&d, 0, sizeof(d));
	d.out_ctx = &bo;
	d.emit = block_put;
	if (lzma_dec_reset(&d, lc, lp, pb, dict_size, &bo, block_put))
		return E_MEM;
	if (lzma_dec_alloc_dict(&d, dict_size))
		return E_MEM;
	if (lzma_dec_alloc_probs(&d))
		return E_MEM;
	lz1_ctx ctx;
	ctx.fr = fr;
	rd_init(&d.src, lz1_fill, &ctx);
	d.out_limit = known_size == UINT64_MAX ? 0 : known_size;
	d.expect_end_marker = known_size == UINT64_MAX;

	int ret = lzma_dec_run(&d);
	if (getenv("XZ_DEBUG"))
		fprintf(stderr, "lzma1_stream_decode: ret=%d dict_pos=%llu buf_pos=%zu\n",
			ret, (unsigned long long)d.dict_pos, d.buf_pos);
	if (ret == E_OK)
		ret = E_DATA;
	if (ret == E_BUF && d.dict_pos == known_size)
		ret = E_STREAM_END;
	lzma_dec_flush_out(&d);
	lzma_dec_free_dict(&d);
	if (ret != E_STREAM_END)
		return ret;
	if (getenv("XZ_DEBUG"))
		fprintf(stderr, "before final block_flush: bo.len=%zu\n", bo.len);
	if (block_flush(&bo))
		return E_MEM;
	/* push back unread bytes */
	{
		const size_t left = d.src.len - d.src.pos;
		if (left > 0) {
			uint8_t tmp[8192];
			memcpy(tmp, d.src.buf + d.src.pos, left);
			if (fr_push(fr, tmp, left))
				return E_DATA;
		}
	}
	return E_OK;
}

/* Legacy .lzma / lzip .lz header decode */
int
lzma1_file_decode(file_r *fr, sink *out, int is_lzip, int nofilter)
{
	uint8_t hdr[13];
	int ret = fr_read_exact(fr, hdr, is_lzip ? 13 : 13);
	if (ret)
		return ret;
	if (is_lzip) {
		if (memcmp(hdr, "LZMA", 4))
			return E_FORMAT;
	} else {
		const uint32_t props = hdr[0];
		if (props >= 9 * 5 * 5)
			return E_OPTIONS;
	}
	uint32_t lc, lp, pb;
	uint32_t dict_size;
	if (is_lzip) {
		lc = 3; lp = 0; pb = 2;
		const uint8_t b = hdr[4];
		if (b > 0xE5)
			return E_OPTIONS;
		dict_size = b == 0 ? 0 : (2 | (b & 1)) << (b / 2 + 11);
	} else {
		const uint32_t props = hdr[0];
		lc = props % 9;
		const uint32_t rem = props / 9;
		lp = rem % 5;
		pb = rem / 5;
		dict_size = (uint32_t)hdr[1] | ((uint32_t)hdr[2] << 8)
			| ((uint32_t)hdr[3] << 16) | ((uint32_t)hdr[4] << 24);
	}
	uint64_t uncomp_size = 0;
	for (int i = 0; i < 8; ++i)
		uncomp_size |= (uint64_t)hdr[5 + i] << (8 * i);
	return lzma1_stream_decode(fr, out, lc, lp, pb, dict_size, uncomp_size,
			nofilter);
}

  preservation, sparse output on decompression.

  filters are stubs (only x86 partially).

  for the two size VLIs, index, footer), `.lzma` and `--format=raw` (LZMA1/LZMA2).
  For simple data the output is byte-identical to the reference (verified for
  an empty file and `hello world\n` with `-T0`).

  matched-literal "break on mismatch" rule; the probability table layout that
  was verified against reference files is
  `is_match[192], is_rep[12], is_rep0[192], is_rep0_long[192], is_rep1[12],
   is_rep2[12], pos_slot[64], pos_special[16371], pos_align[16], len_choice,
   len_low[16][8], len_choice2, len_mid[16][8], len_high[256], literal[]`
  (literal probabilities kept in a separate array).
- List mode (`-l`) reproduces the reference layout for single-stream files.

1. **LZMA decode diverges on data that contains matches.**  Files compressed by
   the reference that contain match symbols fail with
   "Compressed data is corrupt"/"Unexpected end of input"; literal-only data

   LZMA2 chunk).  The divergence was traced to the range/probability state
   drifting apart; probable causes to investigate next:

     `is_rep*` arrays (brute force over offsets found no match), and/or
   - the rep-match state machine (which reps are rotated when).

   symbol; the divergence is a few hundred bytes into the stream.

   implemented; `--filters=x86 ...` will not produce correct data.

   block chain); the block size default is `3 * dict_size`.

   threaded decompression are accepted but not fully honoured.

   the exact props byte validation of the reference could not be determined
   (only props 0/1 were accepted by the reference).

`./compile.sh` -> `gcc -O2 -std=gnu11 -Wall -o executable src/*.c -lm`
(no external dependencies).
